projectedObliquity.source: Hooton et al. (2022), A&A 658, A75 (arXiv:2109.05031), Table 5: sky-projected spin-orbit angle lambda = -69.2 +3.1/-3.4 degrees from the CHEOPS and Spitzer transits, with a prior from the Doppler tomography of Talens et al. (2017). The paper measures the orbital plane anti-clockwise from the stellar equatorial plane (section 4.1), and its transits and tomography do not tell {b, i*, lambda} from {-b, -i*, -lambda}.

stellarInclination.source: Hooton et al. (2022), Table 5: i* = 55.5 +2.3/-2.9 degrees, the angle between the stellar rotation axis and the line of sight (section 4.1), which is this record's convention (90 equator-on).

trueObliquity.source: Hooton et al. (2022), Table 5 and section 7.1: Psi = 72.1 +2.5/-2.4 degrees; the larger side is the tolerance.

equatorialRotationPeriod.source: Hooton et al. (2022), Table 5, derived parameters: stellar rotational period P_rot = 0.853 +0.017/-0.016 days.

source: The star's spin axis measured against MASCARA-1 b's orbit (Hooton et al. (2022), A&A 658, A75): the pole is built in the planet's sky frame from lambda and i*, with the orbit from packages/astronomy/data/bodies/mascara-1b.json, and the star turns once every 0.853 days. The record's lambda, i* and the orbit's 88.45 degree inclination give psi 72.1 degrees, the published 72.1 +2.5/-2.4 degrees.
coordinateSystem: ICRF/J2000. +Z is the measured spin axis; +X faces the Sun at the scene epoch, so grid longitude 0 faces Earth; east longitude. The whole surface turns at one rate.
qualification: The orbit is tilted 72 degrees from the star's equator. The axis's position angle on the sky is not measured; it is placed relative to the planet's orbit, whose orientation on the sky is a display convention (ascending node at position angle 0). The mirrored solution the paper cannot tell from this one is not drawn. The gravity-darkened surface is symmetric about the axis, so the turning is not visible.
